g.text: Stage39: fixed front / shared cells versus separate rear boards
Proposal only. A preferred for source development; no routed, installed or physical qualification.
A — continuous existing JL substrate
40 jacks in four affected columns; all row seams fail.
No seam here: retain JL, including foreign ownership.
2 identical circuit cells; 0 removable mult modules.
No added mult signal/power cables or mount holes.
No extra board depth; shared-board service remains.
B — active front + identical rear23 boards
B1 and B2:32 ×56.5 mm rear boards;34 mm translation.
13 packages/cell remain front;23 move rear.
2 signal +2 power ribbons /8 mating actions.
Shared front tabs and4 new support sites proposed.
Front header fails selector envelope; anchors unresolved.
Electrical boundary and depth consequences
A keeps raw input, protected/sense nodes, precision feedback and complete LED driver on one board.
B passive adapter rejected: a front LED exports the indicator loop. Active front keeps that nine-package loop local.
B signal10: input +3 outputs +buffered monitor, each with AGND. Local rear feedback senses before cable losses.
B front substrate z10–11.6 → cable/support unknown volume → rear z40–41.6 → component/cover unknown volume.
Extra30 mm separation is explicit, unadopted. Enclosure-depth increase cannot be computed from unknown maximum Z.
Neither proposal changes locked positions,0.5 mm copper-edge rules, other-family circuits or canonical manufacturing outputs.
Selection: A is simpler and resolves the seam without new analog interfaces. Interchangeable modules remain a tradeoff.
